newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander ends Latam spree with Brazil buy.
newsitem.headline: Santander ends Latam spree with Brazil buy.

text.p: Spain's leading bank Santander wrapped up an aggressive buying spree in Latin America on Friday with a key purchase in the continent's prize market, Brazil.
Santander said its Banco de Geral unit would buy a 50 percent controlling stake of fellow private Brazilian bank, Noroeste , for an estimated $500 million.
"With this operation Grupo Santander's programme of investments in Latin America is broadly complete," Santander's chairman Emilio Botin said in a statement.
The purchase fortifies Santander's position as the biggest international financial groups in the continent, putting it well ahead of its closest rival, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya .

"This purchase marks the last link in the Latin American franchise of the group. It is definitively the last building block and confirms the bank's place among the top groups in the continent," said an analyst from a U.S. house.

Santander has lead a frenzied drive into Latin America ploughing more than $3 billion into the continent in an effort to diversify in the face of narrowing domestic profit margins and dwindling revenues tied to the launch of Europe's single currency.
The group now owns nine commercial banks and seven investment arms spread across 14 countries, which employ more people than in Spain.

Santander's Latin American expansion has already begun to bear fruit and the bank expects to rake in a $400 million profit from its Latin American holdings in 1997. The bank has said it eventually hopes to have 50 percent of its earnings from the continent.
However, analysts said Santander must now get to work consolidating what they have to ensure they can deliver the promised returns.
"It possible from now on that there will be modest focus downsizing of some of the group's operations," said Alan Broughton, equity analyst at Morgan Stanley in London.
"There could be some possible equity quotations and part-sales of some of their pre-existing operations," he said.
In terms of Santander's share price, analysts said they were cheered by the fact that the Spanish bank would not be coughing up the capital for the purchase.
Santander said given Geral's balance sheet strength and in the light of preliminary due diligence, Geral would not need extra capital from Santander to complete the operation.
Analysts were also cheered that Santander had shut the door on its whirlwind buying binge with an acquisition in Brazil, the leading market in Latin America, which fellow bank BBV has yet to enter.
Santander's Latin America investments contributed 22.52 billion pesetas ($145 million) to earnings in the first quarter.

Taking into account the payment of goodwill and financial costs, Latin American profits attributable to the group represented some 17 percent of group net attributable earnings of 59.78 billion pesetas.
